changes: Śivadeva confidence lowered from high to medium: a lacuna follows the name ('śivadeva . . . . . ja sudhimān'). The gap may have held more of the name, e.g. dvija, or a patronymic, and 'rājasūnu' could mean 'son of Rāja-…' as well as 'prince'.

date.as_written: śrīśākavāṇanidhiṣaḍvidhuge ... somena yukta śubhavāruṇabhe navabhyāṃ krodhisamvatsara

notes: The chronogram vāṇa (5), nidhi (9), ṣaḍ (6), vidhu (1) is read right to left, giving Śaka 1695, i.e. about 1773/74 CE. This matches the catalogue field. 'gelileṣa' is probably 'ge lilekha', with ṣa written for kha ('wrote'). The samvatsara is given as 'krodhi(n)'. In the southern 60-year cycle Śaka 1695 is Vijaya, and Krodhin falls in Śaka 1706 (1784/85 CE). This may be a mismatch, or the scribe used a different reckoning of the cycle. The colophon has lacunae in the scribal verse ('yādṛśaṃ ... ') and after 'śivadeva' ('. . . . . ja sudhimān'). 'rājasūnu' may mean 'prince' or may be part of a patronymic. The month and pakṣa are not stated. The final clause 'svarodayapustakaṃ ca' has no verb that survives.
